headline: Residents across the political divide in a Pennsylvania township are fighting a $165 million data-centre project that emails linked to Amazon.
score_reason: Kept at 5: an 11 Oct 2026 feature on a live local fight with outside figures, from one outlet.
importance_line: It matters to people living near proposed data centres, who are organising across party lines, then to candidates in next month's elections, including Pennsylvania's race for governor, and to developers, but the poll and project counts come from outside groups and Amazon has not confirmed it is the user.
summary: Fortune reports that residents of both parties in Hazle and Sugarloaf townships, Pennsylvania, are fighting a proposed 1,300-acre data centre known as Project Hazelnut, part of a $165 million investment by the developer NorthPoint Development, and the high-voltage power line meant to serve it; emails cited by Fortune name Amazon as the intended user, but an Amazon spokesperson said the company is "evaluating multiple sites across the Commonwealth" and has no definitive agreement. Fortune ties the fight to a wider backlash, citing a Gallup poll in which about 70 percent of Americans oppose local data-centre construction and a Data Center Watch report that at least 75 projects worth over $130 billion were delayed or cancelled in the first quarter of 2026, and says Governor Josh Shapiro has since ended fast-track permits for them.
notes: Feature piece; no news event dated before the window besides Shapiro's August order, which is background.
